title: Suspension of a coefficient section is its shift
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $B_1\leftarrow B_2\leftarrow\cdots$ an inverse sequence of sheaves of commutative rings. Give the category of unbounded cochain complexes of $B_n$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] the flat model structure of [lem-coef-sheaf-flat-model] for every $n$. Assume that for all $i\ge j$ extension of scalars $F_{ij}=B_j\otimes_{B_i}-$ and restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] form a differential graded Quillen adjunction, with the ordinary tensor associators and units as the coherent composition isomorphisms. Let $\operatorname{Sect}$ be the category of strict sections of this diagram, with the projective differential graded model structure of [lem-coef-quillen-section-rectification]: an object is a family of complexes $Q_n$ with structure maps $B_n\otimes_{B_{n+1}}Q_{n+1}\to Q_n$ satisfying the composition identities, and weak equivalences and fibrations are the componentwise quasi-isomorphisms and fibrations. Let $Q$ be a cofibrant object of $\operatorname{Sect}$. Write $Q[1]$ for the componentwise shift, $Q[1]_n^k=Q_n^{k+1}$ with differential $-d$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and $CQ=\operatorname{Cone}(1_Q)$ for the componentwise cone, $(CQ)_n^k=Q_n^{k+1}\oplus Q_n^k$ with differential $(x,y)\mapsto(-dx,x+dy)$ and the structure maps induced from those of $Q$; let $Q\to CQ$ be $y\mapsto(0,y)$. Let $P=CQ\coprod_Q CQ$ be the ordinary pushout of two copies of $Q\to CQ$; at level $n$ and degree $k$ it is $Q_n^{k+1}\oplus Q_n^{k+1}\oplus Q_n^k$ with differential $(x_1,x_2,y)\mapsto(-dx_1,-dx_2,x_1+x_2+dy)$. Then $P$ represents the homotopy pushout of $0\leftarrow Q\to0$, that is the suspension $\Sigma Q$ in the sense of [lem-coef-pointed-model-stability], and the projection $P\to Q[1]$, $(x_1,x_2,y)\mapsto x_2$, is a componentwise quasi-isomorphism of sections, natural in maps of cofibrant sections. Consequently the suspension functor induced on the ordinary homotopy category of $\operatorname{Sect}$ is naturally isomorphic to $[1]$, and it is an equivalence with inverse $[-1]$.

proof.text: The two cone maps to the displayed object are $j_1(x,y)=(x,0,y)$ and $j_2(x,y)=(0,x,y)$. They are chain maps for the displayed differential and agree on $Q$. Given chain maps $a_1,a_2:CQ\to T$ agreeing on $Q$, write their degreewise components as $a_r(x,y)=u_r(x)+v(y)$; then the unique induced map is $(x_1,x_2,y)\mapsto u_1(x_1)+u_2(x_2)+v(y)$. The chain-map equations for $a_1,a_2$ imply the chain-map equation for this formula, and their section compatibilities imply its section compatibility, since the structure maps act separately on the three summands. Thus this is the pushout in $\operatorname{Sect}$. The differential follows from $d j_r=j_r d$; its square is zero because the third component of $d^2$ is $-dx_1-dx_2+d(x_1+x_2+dy)=0$. This verifies both the universal property and the asserted coordinates without any exactness assumption on extension of scalars.

proof.text: The cone lemma gives that $Q\to CQ$ is a cofibration of sections, that $CQ\to0$ is a componentwise quasi-isomorphism, and that its cokernel is $Q[1]$. Since $Q$ is cofibrant, $0\to Q$ is a cofibration; model-category cofibrations are closed under composition, so $0\to CQ$ is a cofibration and $CQ$ is cofibrant. Thus the span $CQ\leftarrow Q\to CQ$ has cofibrant objects and cofibration legs.

proof.text: The projection $p:P\to Q[1]$, $(x_1,x_2,y)\mapsto x_2$, is a chain map because the second component of the differential on $P$ is $-dx_2$, which is the differential of the shifted complex. It is a map of sections by construction. It is degreewise surjective, and its kernel is the subcomplex with $x_2=0$, identified with $CQ$ by $(x_1,y)\mapsto(x_1,0,y)$. Hence there is a short exact sequence of complexes $0\to CQ\to P\xrightarrow{p}Q[1]\to0$ at every section level. Since $CQ\to0$ is a quasi-isomorphism, the long exact cohomology sequence for this short exact sequence shows that $p$ is a componentwise quasi-isomorphism. The same formulas commute with maps of cofibrant sections, so $p$ is natural.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-pointed-model-stability] to $\operatorname{Sect}$: its zero object is the zero section, and its model structure is the one in the hypotheses. By Step 2 the ordinary pushout $P$ represents the homotopy pushout of $CQ\leftarrow Q\to CQ$. In the localization the maps $CQ\to0$ are equivalences, so this span is equivalent, by a transformation which is the identity on $Q$, to $0\leftarrow Q\to0$. Their colimits are therefore equivalent by the colimit universal property. Consequently $P$ represents $\Sigma Q$. These comparisons are natural: for $f:Q\to Q'$ the maps are $Cf(x,y)=(f(x),f(y))$ and $Pf(x_1,x_2,y)=(f(x_1),f(x_2),f(y))$; both commute with the cone inclusions and the maps to zero, while $p_{Q'}Pf=f[1]p_Q$.

proof.text: For an arbitrary section $X$, choose functorial cofibrant replacement $q_X:RX\to X$ from the given projective model structure. The functor $[1]$ preserves componentwise quasi-isomorphisms since $H^k(X[1]_n)=H^{k+1}(X_n)$; thus $q_X[1]$ is a weak equivalence. Steps 3--4 give the natural zigzag $\Sigma X\simeq P(RX)\xrightarrow{p_{RX}}RX[1]\xrightarrow{q_X[1]}X[1]$ in the ordinary homotopy category, which is the localization at weak equivalences by [lem-coef-pointed-model-stability]. All arrows are natural and invertible there. Both shifts descend to this localization, and $X[1][-1]=X=X[-1][1]$ on complexes and on section maps (the two differential signs cancel). Thus the induced suspension is naturally isomorphic to $[1]$ and has inverse $[-1]$.
